Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: initialise, configure, read, use the interrupt pin, read NVM and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Driver standing for bmp581::Driver<MyI2c> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One bmp581::Driver<Bus> object per sensor. It holds a reference to your port and the chip id; everything else lives in the chip's registers. Group Calls Registers Lifecycle Init() , SoftReset() , Configure(Config) , ChipId() , Initialized() CHIP_ID, STATUS, CMD, INT_STATUS Power mode GetPowerMode() , SetPowerMode(PowerMode) ODR_CONFIG Oversampling and data rate GetOsrOdr() , SetOsrOdr(OsrOdrConfig) , GetEffectiveOsr() OSR_CONFIG, ODR_CONFIG, OSR_EFF IIR filter GetIir() , SetIir(IirConfig) DSP_CONFIG, DSP_IIR Interrupts ConfigureInterrupt(InterruptConfig) , SelectInterruptSources(InterruptSources) , ReadInterruptStatus() , DataReady() INT_CONFIG, INT_SOURCE, INT_STATUS Data ReadSample(pressure_enabled) , DecodeSample(bytes, pressure_enabled) TEMP_DATA, PRESS_DATA NVM ReadNvm(row) NVM_ADDR, NVM_DATA, CMD Raw access ReadRegister(reg) , WriteRegister(reg, value) any Every call returns bmp581::DriverResult<T> : .value and .error , and it converts to bool . Check it: false means a transfer failed or the chip did not confirm the step. Initialise ¶ bool bring_up ( Driver & dev ) { const auto init = dev . Init (); // chip id 0x50 / 0x51, STATUS.nvm_rdy, no NVM error if ( ! init ) { std :: printf ( "init: %s 
 " , bmp581 :: ToString ( init . error ). data ()); return false ; } const auto reset = dev . SoftReset (); // CMD 0xB6, 2 ms, INT_STATUS.por checked if ( ! reset ) { std :: printf ( "soft reset: %s 
 " , bmp581 :: ToString ( reset . error ). data ()); return false ; } std :: printf ( "BMP581 chip id 0x%02X, driver %s 
 " , dev . ChipId (), bmp581 :: GetDriverVersion ()); return true ; } Init() is safe to call again: it clears ChipId() first and fills it only on success. SoftReset() returns every register to its reset value, so call it before Configure() , never after. Over I2C the chip does not acknowledge the reset command; the port must count that write as sent ( Porting ). Configure ¶ bool configure_low_noise ( Driver & dev ) { bmp581 :: Config cfg {}; cfg . osr_odr . osr_pressure = bmp581 :: Oversampling :: X64 ; cfg . osr_odr . osr_temperature = bmp581 :: Oversampling :: X4 ; cfg . osr_odr . odr = bmp581 :: Odr :: Hz10 ; // datasheet table 7: at most 20 Hz with these OSRs cfg . iir . pressure = bmp581 :: IirFilter :: Coeff7 ; cfg . power_mode = bmp581 :: PowerMode :: Normal ; if ( ! dev . Configure ( cfg )) { // standby, OSR / ODR, IIR, then the power mode return false ; } const auto eff = dev . GetEffectiveOsr (); // the chip falls back to default OSRs if the ODR is too fast return eff && eff . value . odr_valid ; } Configure() writes standby, then oversampling and data rate, then the IIR filter, then the power mode, and stops at the first failure. Pick a pair of oversampling ratios the data rate allows ( Register interface ), then check odr_valid : when it is false the chip runs with default ratios, not yours. Configuration has presets for common uses. Read ¶ bool read_when_ready ( Driver & dev , float & pressure_pa , float & temperature_c ) { const auto ready = dev . DataReady (); // reads INT_STATUS, which clears it if ( ! ready || ! ready . value ) { return false ; // bus error, or no new sample yet } const auto s = dev . ReadSample (); // one 6-byte burst from 0x1D if ( ! s ) { return false ; } pressure_pa = s . value . pressure_pa ; // raw / 64 temperature_c = s . value . temperature_c ; // raw / 65536 return true ; } DataReady() reads INT_STATUS, and reading INT_STATUS clears it. Do not read INT_STATUS anywhere else between two samples, or you lose the flag. ReadSample(false) skips the pressure conversion when you disabled pressure with OsrOdrConfig::pressure_enable = false . Take one sample on demand ¶ bool one_shot ( Driver & dev , MyI2c & bus , bmp581 :: Sample & out ) { if ( ! dev . SetPowerMode ( bmp581 :: PowerMode :: Forced )) { // one conversion, then back to standby return false ; } bus . DelayUs ( bmp581 :: timing :: kStartupUs + 7000U ); // t_startup + conversion at OSR x8 / x1 (6.4 ms) const auto s = dev . ReadSample (); if ( ! s ) { return false ; } out = s . value ; return true ; } Forced mode does one conversion and returns to standby: the lowest average current for slow, irregular sampling. The wait is t_startup (3 ms) plus the conversion time for the oversampling you set (datasheet Table 4). Use the interrupt pin ¶ bool enable_data_ready_pin ( Driver & dev ) { bmp581 :: InterruptConfig pin {}; pin . mode = bmp581 :: IntMode :: Pulsed ; // about 105 us pulse per sample pin . polarity = bmp581 :: IntPolarity :: ActiveHigh ; pin . drive = bmp581 :: IntDrive :: PushPull ; pin . enable = true ; if ( ! dev . ConfigureInterrupt ( pin )) { // disables sources and clears INT_STATUS first return false ; } bmp581 :: InterruptSources src {}; src . data_ready = true ; return dev . SelectInterruptSources ( src ). ok (); } In pulsed mode INT pulses for 90 µs to 121 µs per event; in latched mode it stays active until you read ReadInterruptStatus() . Use open drain when several devices share the line, and pull it up to VDDIO. Read the NVM user words ¶ bool read_user_words ( Driver & dev , uint16_t ( & words )[ 3 ]) { for ( uint8_t i = 0 ; i < 3 ; ++ i ) { const auto w = dev . ReadNvm ( static_cast < uint8_t > ( bmp581 :: nvm :: kStartAddr + i )); // rows 0x20..0x22 if ( ! w ) { return false ; } words [ i ] = w . value ; } return true ; } The NVM holds three 16-bit user words at rows 0x20 to 0x22 . ReadNvm() switches to standby for the read and restores the previous mode. Writing the NVM is not wrapped. Use any register directly ¶ bool read_revision ( Driver & dev , uint8_t & rev ) { const auto r = dev . ReadRegister ( bmp581 :: reg :: kRevId ); // 0x32 on current silicon if ( ! r ) { return false ; } rev = r . value ; return true ; } ReadRegister() and WriteRegister() reach anything the driver does not wrap: FIFO, out-of-range detection, pad drive strength. The addresses and masks are in bmp581_registers.hpp . Write standby-only registers in standby. Handle errors ¶ const char * advice ( bmp581 :: DriverError e ) { switch ( e ) { case bmp581 :: DriverError :: None : return "ok" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: NotInitialized : return "EnsureInitialized() failed: bring the bus up" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: Bus : return "a transfer failed: wiring, address, pull-ups" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: InvalidChipId : return "not a BMP581, or the first SPI read" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: NvmNotReady : return "NVM boot not finished or NVM error" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: PorSoftReset : return "reset not confirmed by INT_STATUS.por" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: NvmInvalidAddr : return "NVM user rows are 0x20..0x22" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: NvmCommandError : return "NVM command rejected (chip not in standby)" ; case bmp581 :: DriverError :: InvalidParameter : case bmp581 :: DriverError :: InvalidPowerMode : return "invalid argument" ; } return "unknown" ; } DriverError Returned by Meaning NotInitialized Init() Your port's EnsureInitialized() returned false Bus any call ReadRegs() or WriteRegs() returned false InvalidChipId Init() CHIP_ID read 0, or not 0x50 / 0x51 NvmNotReady Init() , ReadNvm() nvm_rdy clear or nvm_err set, after one soft-reset retry in Init() PorSoftReset SoftReset() INT_STATUS por not set 2 ms after the reset command NvmInvalidAddr ReadNvm() Row outside 0x20 .. 0x22 NvmCommandError Init() , ReadNvm() nvm_cmd_err : an NVM command outside standby InvalidPowerMode SetPowerMode() A value outside the PowerMode enum ToString(DriverError) returns the enumerator's name for logs. Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the sensor. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one bmp581::Driver object, whose public calls are listed from inc/bmp581_driver.hpp. Each call becomes register reads and writes in the order the datasheet requires (the standby hop, IIR writes in standby, POR and NVM checks). The register transport (BusInterface in inc/bmp581_bus_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base with four methods. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that implements them over I2C or SPI. Below it is the sensor. Drawn from: inc/bmp581_driver.hpp Driver public members ; inc/bmp581_bus_interface.hpp BusInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where Depends on You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : Driver<Bus> inc/bmp581_driver.hpp The transport's four methods Never, for a new board Register transport : BusInterface<Bus> inc/bmp581_bus_interface.hpp Your port Never Platform port : your class Your project Your SDK Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test fake. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the sensor ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as Driver participant P as Your port participant S as BMP581 A->>D: SetIir(cfg) D->>P: ReadRegs(ODR_CONFIG, 1) P->>S: read 0x37 S-->>P: pwr_mode = normal D->>P: WriteRegs(ODR_CONFIG, standby) and DelayUs(2500) D->>P: ReadRegs(DSP_CONFIG, 2) D->>P: WriteRegs(DSP_CONFIG, 2 bytes) P->>S: write 0x30, 0x31 D->>P: WriteRegs(ODR_CONFIG, normal) D-->>A: DriverResult<void> (ok, or Bus) The diagram leaves out the repeated reads of ODR_CONFIG that SetPowerMode() makes to learn the current mode. Configuration writes are read-modify-write: the driver reads the register, changes only its own bits and writes it back, so settings it does not manage (pad drive strength, FIFO, out-of-range) keep their values. Why CRTP ¶ The transport is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: Driver<MyI2c> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too. Results, not exceptions ¶ Every call returns DriverResult<T> : a value and a DriverError . It converts to bool ( true when error == DriverError::None ), and ToString(error) gives a stable name for logs. The driver never throws and never logs; what to do with an error is the application's decision. What the driver does not cover ¶ The FIFO (32 frames), out-of-range pressure detection and NVM programming are not wrapped. The register addresses and bit masks are in bmp581_registers.hpp ; reach them with ReadRegister() and WriteRegister() ( API guide ). docs.text: The transport is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: Driver<MyI2c> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too.

docs.text: Every call returns DriverResult<T> : a value and a DriverError . It converts to bool ( true when error == DriverError::None ), and ToString(error) gives a stable name for logs. The driver never throws and never logs; what to do with an error is the application's decision.

Every snippet here is compiled from tests/docs/configuration.cpp . The preset ¶ bmp581 :: DriverResult < void > use_preset ( bmp581 :: Driver < MyI2c >& dev ) { return dev . Configure ( bmp581 :: BarometricReferencePreset ()); // 100.3 Hz, OSR p x8 / t x1, IIR 3, normal } BarometricReferencePreset() is for a pressure reference sampled by a control loop: pressure oversampling ×8 (0.30 Pa RMS typical), temperature ×1, Odr::Hz100_2 (100.3 Hz; the pair allows up to 140 Hz), IIR coefficient 3 on both channels (-3 dB at about 4.6 Hz), normal mode. docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a BMP581, with which bus settings, and the board-level traps to avoid. All values here come from the Bosch BMP581 datasheet (BST-BMP581-DS004, revision 1.13). Table and section numbers refer to that revision. Pins ¶ The sensor is a 10-pin LGA with pin 1 marked on the lid (datasheet section 6.1, Table 28). Pin Name I2C SPI 1 VDDIO I/O supply I/O supply 2 SCK SCL SCK 3, 8, 9 VSS GND GND 4 SDI SDA MOSI; data in and out in 3-wire mode 5 SDO Address: GND 0x46, VDDIO 0x47 MISO; leave floating in 3-wire mode 6 CSB Tie to VDDIO Chip select, active low 7 INT Interrupt output Interrupt output 10 VDD Analog supply Analog supply If you do not use INT, connect it to GND and leave the interrupt disabled (the reset state of INT_CONFIG.int_en is 0). Interface selection ¶ The sensor chooses its interface from CSB, not from a strap (datasheet section 5.1): After power-up or a soft reset it is in I2C / I3C mode. With CSB held at VDDIO it stays there. The first SPI transaction (CSB low, at least 16 SCK edges, CSB high) switches it to SPI until the next power-down or soft reset. That transaction's data is invalid: do one dummy read first. 3-wire SPI is selected by DRIVE_CONFIG.spi3_en = 1 , written over 4-wire SPI. The porting SPI port does the dummy read in EnsureInitialized() and again after a soft reset. Bus settings ¶ Setting I2C SPI Mode Standard (100 kHz), fast (400 kHz), fast-mode plus (1 MHz) Mode 0 or mode 3, detected from SCK at the CSB falling edge Speed Up to 1 MHz (bus capacitance under 550 pF; under 100 pF for 1 MHz) Up to 12 MHz with VDDIO ≥ 1.62 V; 7 MHz below Address / select 7-bit 0x46 (SDO low) or 0x47 (SDO high) CSB, active low Write [addr+W] [reg] [data...] , register address increments One [reg & 0x7F] [data] pair per byte: no auto-increment on SPI writes Read [addr+W] [reg] , repeated START, [addr+R] [data...] [reg | 0x80] , then the data bytes, no dummy byte Burst reads Address increments after each byte Same Two exceptions from the datasheet matter for a port: A write of the soft-reset command (CMD 0x7E = 0xB6) over I2C is not acknowledged (section 7.36). Treat it as sent. After writing DRIVE_CONFIG, INT_CONFIG or the NVM data registers, keep CSB high for at least 1 µs before reading them back (section 5.5.4). sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant S as BMP581 H->>S: write ODR_CONFIG = standby Note over S: t_standby, up to 2.5 ms H->>S: write OSR_CONFIG, ODR_CONFIG (OSR, ODR) H->>S: write DSP_CONFIG, DSP_IIR (filter, standby only) H->>S: write ODR_CONFIG = normal Note over S: t_startup, up to 3 ms, then one conversion per ODR period H->>S: read INT_STATUS S-->>H: drdy_data_reg = 1 (reading clears it) H->>S: burst read 0x1D..0x22 S-->>H: temperature (3 bytes), pressure (3 bytes) Timing ¶ Event Symbol Maximum Source Power-up to first communication t_powup 2 ms Table 4 Standby to start of measurement t_startup 3 ms Table 4 Deep standby to start of measurement t_startup_deep 4 ms Table 4 Any mode to standby t_standby 2.5 ms Table 4 Soft reset t_soft_res 2 ms Table 4 Pressure conversion, OSR ×1 / ×8 / ×128 t_conv_p 1.0 / 5.4 / 80.4 ms typical Table 4 INT pulse in pulsed mode t_int_pulse 90 to 121 µs Table 4 The driver waits these times through DelayUs() ; the constants are in bmp581::timing . Power ¶ Supply Range Notes VDD (analog) 1.71 V to 3.6 V 100 nF to ground VDDIO (interface) 1.08 V to 3.6 V 100 nF to ground; sets the logic levels of every interface pin Ramp time 0.01 ms to 10 ms (10 % to 90 %) Faster ramps (direct battery connection): add 10 Ω in series with each supply The supplies can come up in either order. Current is 1.3 µA at 1 Hz in the lowest-power setting and 75 µA typical at 30 Hz with high-resolution oversampling (Table 4). Do not drive interface pins while VDDIO is off A logic high on SDI, SDO, SCK or CSB while VDDIO is switched off can damage the sensor through its ESD diodes (datasheet section 4.2). Power the sensor from the same rail as the MCU's I/O, or tri-state the bus first. Placement for a pressure reference ¶ Vent the sensor to the volume you want to measure, away from fans and heat sources. The offset changes by ±0.5 Pa/K (Table 1), so thermal stability matters more than sampling rate. Reflow shifts the offset by about ±30 Pa (solder drift, Table 1). When absolute accuracy matters, compare against a reference once after assembly. Performance ¶ Parameter Value Conditions Pressure range 30 to 125 kPa Absolute accuracy ±30 Pa typical 300 to 1100 hPa, -5 to 65 °C Relative accuracy ±6 Pa typical 700 to 1100 hPa, 15 to 55 °C, 10 kPa steps Noise 0.08 Pa RMS typical Highest-resolution oversampling Temperature accuracy ±0.5 K typical -40 to 85 °C Output data rate 0.125 to 240 Hz Normal mode; continuous mode up to 480 Hz Breakout boards ¶ Board Connectors Interfaces SparkFun SEN-20170 Two Qwiic, 0.1 in. header I2C (default address 0x47, alternative 0x46) or SPI Adafruit 6407 Two STEMMA QT, 8-pin header I2C or SPI The ESP32 examples use I2C0 on GPIO 8 (SDA) and 9 (SCL) at 400 kHz with address 0x47; see Examples . docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++17 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++17 compiler: GCC 9+, Clang 10+ or the ESP-IDF toolchains. CMake 3.16 or newer, if you use the CMake target. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call is noexcept and returns a DriverResult . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-bmp581-driver.git external/hf-bmp581-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-bmp581-driver Only inc/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-bmp581-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::bmp581 ) hf::bmp581 (alias of hf_bmp581 ) is an INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories, including the folder with the generated bmp581_version.h , and requires C++17 ( cxx_std_17 ). Option Default Effect HF_BMP581_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on targets that link the driver HF_BMP581_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests and the documentation snippets ( Testing and CI ) Without add_subdirectory , include the settings file and use its variables: include ( external/hf-bmp581-driver/cmake/hf_bmp581_build_settings.cmake ) target_include_directories ( my_app PRIVATE ${ HF_BMP581_PUBLIC_INCLUDE_DIRS } ) target_compile_features ( my_app PRIVATE cxx_std_17 ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_bmp581/ . docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the register transport, over I2C or SPI. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls four methods on a class you derive from bmp581::BusInterface<Self> (in inc/bmp581_bus_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one bmp581::Driver object, whose public calls are listed from inc/bmp581_driver.hpp. Each call becomes register reads and writes in the order the datasheet requires (the standby hop, IIR writes in standby, POR and NVM checks). The register transport (BusInterface in inc/bmp581_bus_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base with four methods. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that implements them over I2C or SPI. Below it is the sensor. Drawn from: inc/bmp581_driver.hpp Driver public members ; inc/bmp581_bus_interface.hpp BusInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Contract bool WriteRegs(uint8_t reg, const uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) Write len bytes to reg , reg + 1 , ... Return false on a bus error. The driver writes at most 2 bytes at a time bool ReadRegs(uint8_t reg, uint8_t* out, std::size_t len) Read len bytes from reg onwards into out . The driver reads at most 6 bytes at a time void DelayUs(uint32_t us) Block for at least us microseconds. The driver asks for 800 µs to 5 ms bool EnsureInitialized() Return true when the bus is ready. Init() calls it first and fails with NotInitialized otherwise All four must be noexcept -compatible: the driver's calls are noexcept . I2C port ¶ my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public bmp581 :: BusInterface < MyI2c > { public : // 7-bit address: 0x46 with SDO low, 0x47 with SDO high. explicit MyI2c ( uint8_t address = bmp581 :: addr :: kSecondary ) noexcept : address_ ( address ) {} // One transaction: [reg, data...]. The chip increments the register address after each byte. bool WriteRegs ( uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t frame [ 16 ]; if ( len + 1 > sizeof ( frame )) { return false ; } frame [ 0 ] = reg ; std :: memcpy ( frame + 1 , data , len ); const bool acked = platform_i2c_write ( address_ , frame , len + 1 ); // The BMP581 does not acknowledge a soft-reset command over I2C: count that write as sent. const bool soft_reset = reg == bmp581 :: reg :: kCmd && len == 1 && data [ 0 ] == bmp581 :: cmd :: kSoftReset ; return acked || soft_reset ; } // Write the register address, repeated START, read len bytes (auto-increment). bool ReadRegs ( uint8_t reg , uint8_t * out , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( address_ , & reg , 1 , out , len ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Called before every Init(); bring the bus up here if your SDK needs it. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return true ; } private : uint8_t address_ ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One transaction per call. A write is START, address, register, data, STOP. A read is START, address, register, repeated START (or STOP and START), address, data, STOP. Count a soft reset as sent. The chip does not acknowledge the data byte when CMD (0x7E) is written with 0xB6 (datasheet section 7.36). If your SDK reports the missing acknowledge as an error and the port passes it on, SoftReset() returns Bus and Init() cannot recover a part whose NVM boot did not finish. Do not let SDO float. It sets the address bit; floating, the address is undefined. SPI port ¶ my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public bmp581 :: BusInterface < MySpi > { public : // SPI writes do not auto-increment: send one (address, data) pair per byte, bit 7 clear. bool WriteRegs ( uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t tx [ 16 ]; uint8_t rx [ 16 ]; if ( 2 * len > sizeof ( tx )) { return false ; } for ( std :: size_t i = 0 ; i < len ; ++ i ) { tx [ 2 * i ] = static_cast < uint8_t > (( reg + i ) & 0x7FU ); tx [ 2 * i + 1 ] = data [ i ]; } if ( ! platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , 2 * len )) { return false ; } if ( reg == bmp581 :: reg :: kCmd && data [ 0 ] == bmp581 :: cmd :: kSoftReset ) { // A soft reset returns the interface to I2C mode; one dummy read selects SPI again. platform_delay_us ( bmp581 :: timing :: kSoftResetUs ); return DummyRead (); } return true ; } // Reads: address with bit 7 set, then the data bytes (auto-increment); no dummy byte. bool ReadRegs ( uint8_t reg , uint8_t * out , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t tx [ 16 ] = {}; uint8_t rx [ 16 ] = {}; if ( len + 1 > sizeof ( tx )) { return false ; } tx [ 0 ] = static_cast < uint8_t > ( reg | 0x80U ); if ( ! platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len + 1 )) { return false ; } for ( std :: size_t i = 0 ; i < len ; ++ i ) { out [ i ] = rx [ i + 1 ]; } return true ; } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // The chip powers up in I2C mode. The first SPI read switches it to SPI; its data is invalid. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! spi_selected_ ) { spi_selected_ = DummyRead (); } return spi_selected_ ; } private : bool DummyRead () noexcept { uint8_t tx [ 2 ] = { static_cast < uint8_t > ( bmp581 :: reg :: kChipId | 0x80U ), 0 }; uint8_t rx [ 2 ] = {}; return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , sizeof ( tx )); } bool spi_selected_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: SPI mode 0 or 3 , MSB first, up to 12 MHz (7 MHz with VDDIO under 1.62 V). Writes do not auto-increment. Send an address byte (bit 7 clear) before every data byte, as the datasheet's burst-write figure shows. The driver writes two consecutive registers in SetOsrOdr() and SetIir() . Reads set bit 7 of the address and return data from the next byte on, with auto-increment. Select SPI with a dummy read after power-up and after every soft reset: both return the chip to I2C mode, and the read that switches it returns invalid data. I2C SPI Call from the driver Bytes on the bus WriteRegs(0x36, {a, b}, 2) [0x47 W] 0x36 a b ReadRegs(0x1D, out, 6) [0x47 W] 0x1D [0x47 R] t0 t1 t2 p0 p1 p2 Call from the driver Bytes on the bus (CSB low for each line) WriteRegs(0x36, {a, b}, 2) 0x36 a 0x37 b ReadRegs(0x1D, out, 6) 0x9D then six bytes clocked in: t0 t1 t2 p0 p1 p2 Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use hf_bmp581_esp_i2c.hpp : Bmp581EspIdfI2c<port, sda, scl, address, speed> , an I2C port on the legacy ESP-IDF driver/i2c.h API with FreeRTOS delays. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target, and add the soft-reset exception above. Check your port ¶ Build it: both ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call Init() and print ChipId() : 0x50 proves register reads end to end. Call SoftReset() : ok() proves the CMD write, the reset wait and (on SPI) the dummy read. Call Configure() , then GetOsrOdr() : reading back what you wrote proves two-byte writes. Read a few samples: about 101 kPa at sea level, falling by about 12 Pa per metre of height. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each sensor one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. Several sensors on separate ports, or at both addresses of one I2C bus, can run in parallel as long as the bus driver serialises transactions.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Read pressure and temperature from your MCU: wire four signals, write a small port class, call four driver functions. 1. Wire it ¶ The quickstart uses I2C, the interface the sensor selects after power-up. Hardware has the SPI wiring and the full pin list. MCU BMP581 Notes 3.3 V (or 1.8 V) VDD (pin 10), VDDIO (pin 1) 100 nF to ground on each GND VSS (pins 3, 8, 9) I2C SCL SCK (pin 2) Pull-up to VDDIO; up to 1 MHz, start at 400 kHz I2C SDA SDI (pin 4) Pull-up to VDDIO VDDIO or GND SDO (pin 5) High: address 0x47; low: 0x46. Do not leave it floating VDDIO CSB (pin 6) Keeps the sensor in I2C mode Breakout boards such as the SparkFun SEN-20170 (default address 0x47) and the Adafruit 6407 carry the pull-ups; check the board's jumpers for the address. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf::bmp581 CMake target (or add inc/ to your include path and build with C++17). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-bmp581-driver.git external/hf-bmp581-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. It writes and reads registers and waits. Replace the three platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public bmp581 :: BusInterface < MyI2c > { public : // 7-bit address: 0x46 with SDO low, 0x47 with SDO high. explicit MyI2c ( uint8_t address = bmp581 :: addr :: kSecondary ) noexcept : address_ ( address ) {} // One transaction: [reg, data...]. The chip increments the register address after each byte. bool WriteRegs ( uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t frame [ 16 ]; if ( len + 1 > sizeof ( frame )) { return false ; } frame [ 0 ] = reg ; std :: memcpy ( frame + 1 , data , len ); const bool acked = platform_i2c_write ( address_ , frame , len + 1 ); // The BMP581 does not acknowledge a soft-reset command over I2C: count that write as sent. const bool soft_reset = reg == bmp581 :: reg :: kCmd && len == 1 && data [ 0 ] == bmp581 :: cmd :: kSoftReset ; return acked || soft_reset ; } // Write the register address, repeated START, read len bytes (auto-increment). bool ReadRegs ( uint8_t reg , uint8_t * out , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( address_ , & reg , 1 , out , len ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Called before every Init(); bring the bus up here if your SDK needs it. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return true ; } private : uint8_t address_ ; }; Porting explains each method and shows the SPI variant. 4. Read the sensor ¶ main.cpp #include "bmp581.hpp" #include <cstdio> int read_pressure_once ( MyI2c & bus ) { bmp581 :: Driver < MyI2c > dev ( bus ); if ( const auto r = dev . Init (); ! r ) { // 1. chip id and NVM ready std :: printf ( "init: %s \n " , bmp581 :: ToString ( r . error ). data ()); return -1 ; // wiring, address or supply } if ( ! dev . Configure ( bmp581 :: BarometricReferencePreset ())) { // 2. 100 Hz, OSR x8, IIR 3, normal mode return -1 ; } for ( int i = 0 ; i < 50 ; ++ i ) { // 3. wait for the first conversion const auto ready = dev . DataReady (); if ( ! ready || ready . value ) break ; bus . DelayUs ( 1000 ); } const auto s = dev . ReadSample (); // 4. pressure (Pa) and temperature (C) if ( ! s ) return -1 ; std :: printf ( "%.1f Pa %.2f C \n " , static_cast < double > ( s . value . pressure_pa ), static_cast < double > ( s . value . temperature_c )); return 0 ; } What each step does: Init() reads CHIP_ID (0x50) and checks that the NVM has loaded ( STATUS.nvm_rdy , no nvm_err ). Nothing else is worth calling until it succeeds. Configure() puts the chip in standby, writes oversampling and output data rate, then the IIR filter, then switches to normal mode. The preset samples at 100 Hz with pressure oversampling ×8. DataReady() reads INT_STATUS until the first conversion is done, about 10 ms after the mode change. ReadSample() reads the six data registers in one burst and converts them: pressure / 64 in pascals, temperature / 65536 in degrees Celsius. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. docs.text: The quickstart uses I2C, the interface the sensor selects after power-up. Hardware has the SPI wiring and the full pin list. MCU BMP581 Notes 3.3 V (or 1.8 V) VDD (pin 10), VDDIO (pin 1) 100 nF to ground on each GND VSS (pins 3, 8, 9) I2C SCL SCK (pin 2) Pull-up to VDDIO; up to 1 MHz, start at 400 kHz I2C SDA SDI (pin 4) Pull-up to VDDIO VDDIO or GND SDO (pin 5) High: address 0x47; low: 0x46. Do not leave it floating VDDIO CSB (pin 6) Keeps the sensor in I2C mode Breakout boards such as the SparkFun SEN-20170 (default address 0x47) and the Adafruit 6407 carry the pull-ups; check the board's jumpers for the address.

docs.text: The port is the only platform code. It writes and reads registers and waits. Replace the three platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public bmp581 :: BusInterface < MyI2c > { public : // 7-bit address: 0x46 with SDO low, 0x47 with SDO high. explicit MyI2c ( uint8_t address = bmp581 :: addr :: kSecondary ) noexcept : address_ ( address ) {} // One transaction: [reg, data...]. The chip increments the register address after each byte. bool WriteRegs ( uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t frame [ 16 ]; if ( len + 1 > sizeof ( frame )) { return false ; } frame [ 0 ] = reg ; std :: memcpy ( frame + 1 , data , len ); const bool acked = platform_i2c_write ( address_ , frame , len + 1 ); // The BMP581 does not acknowledge a soft-reset command over I2C: count that write as sent. const bool soft_reset = reg == bmp581 :: reg :: kCmd && len == 1 && data [ 0 ] == bmp581 :: cmd :: kSoftReset ; return acked || soft_reset ; } // Write the register address, repeated START, read len bytes (auto-increment). bool ReadRegs ( uint8_t reg , uint8_t * out , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( address_ , & reg , 1 , out , len ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Called before every Init(); bring the bus up here if your SDK needs it. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return true ; } private : uint8_t address_ ; }; Porting explains each method and shows the SPI variant.
docs.title: 3. Write the port

docs.text: main.cpp #include "bmp581.hpp" #include <cstdio> int read_pressure_once ( MyI2c & bus ) { bmp581 :: Driver < MyI2c > dev ( bus ); if ( const auto r = dev . Init (); ! r ) { // 1. chip id and NVM ready std :: printf ( "init: %s \n " , bmp581 :: ToString ( r . error ). data ()); return -1 ; // wiring, address or supply } if ( ! dev . Configure ( bmp581 :: BarometricReferencePreset ())) { // 2. 100 Hz, OSR x8, IIR 3, normal mode return -1 ; } for ( int i = 0 ; i < 50 ; ++ i ) { // 3. wait for the first conversion const auto ready = dev . DataReady (); if ( ! ready || ready . value ) break ; bus . DelayUs ( 1000 ); } const auto s = dev . ReadSample (); // 4. pressure (Pa) and temperature (C) if ( ! s ) return -1 ; std :: printf ( "%.1f Pa %.2f C \n " , static_cast < double > ( s . value . pressure_pa ), static_cast < double > ( s . value . temperature_c )); return 0 ; } What each step does: Init() reads CHIP_ID (0x50) and checks that the NVM has loaded ( STATUS.nvm_rdy , no nvm_err ). Nothing else is worth calling until it succeeds. Configure() puts the chip in standby, writes oversampling and output data rate, then the IIR filter, then switches to normal mode. The preset samples at 100 Hz with pressure oversampling ×8. DataReady() reads INT_STATUS until the first conversion is done, about 10 ms after the mode change. ReadSample() reads the six data registers in one burst and converts them: pressure / 64 in pascals, temperature / 65536 in degrees Celsius. Power modes ¶ stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> DeepStandby: reset DeepStandby --> Standby: deep_dis = 1 Standby --> Normal: 01 Standby --> Forced: 10 Standby --> Continuous: 11 Normal --> Standby: 00 Continuous --> Standby: 00 Forced --> Standby: done The labels are the values written to ODR_CONFIG.pwr_mode ; every transition into standby takes up to t_standby (2.5 ms). Changing any setting deep standby does not allow also moves the chip from deep standby to standby. Mode PowerMode What the chip does Standby Standby No conversions; every register is writable; the data registers keep the last result Deep standby DeepStandby Lower current than standby. Only while deep_dis = 0 , ODR below 5 Hz, FIFO off and both IIR filters bypassed Normal Normal One conversion per ODR period, standby in between Forced Forced One conversion, then standby Continuous Continuous Back-to-back conversions; the ODR setting is ignored Rules the driver follows (datasheet section 4.3): Every change goes through standby. SetPowerMode() writes standby first when the chip is in another mode and waits t_standby (2.5 ms), then writes the target mode. Some registers are writable only in standby , the IIR configuration among them. SetIir() switches to standby, writes, then restores normal, forced or continuous mode. A data rate faster than 5 Hz needs deep standby disabled. SetOsrOdr() writes standby with deep_dis = 1 first when the chip is in deep standby. DeepStandby is a pseudo-mode in the driver: standby with deep_dis = 0 . After power-up or a soft reset the chip is in deep standby ( ODR_CONFIG resets to 0x70 : 1 Hz, deep_dis = 0 ). Oversampling and data rate ¶ Not every pair of oversampling ratios fits in every ODR period. In normal mode the chip checks the pair, sets OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid and, when the pair does not fit, runs with OSR ×1 / ×1 (ODR 160 Hz and up) or ×2 / ×2 (below 160 Hz). Read it with GetEffectiveOsr() . Highest nominal ODR in normal mode (Hz) for each pair (datasheet Table 7): Pressure OSR T ×1 T ×2 T ×4 T ×8 T ×16 T ×32 T ×64 T ×128 ×1 240 240 240 240 200 130 80 40 ×2 240 240 240 220 180 120 70 40 ×4 220 220 200 180 140 100 70 40 ×8 140 140 130 120 100 80 50 35 ×16 80 80 80 70 70 50 45 30 ×32 45 45 40 40 40 35 30 20 ×64 20 20 20 20 20 20 15 15 ×128 10 10 10 10 10 10 10 5 Typical pressure noise at 100 kPa (datasheet Table 9): 0.78 Pa RMS at ×1, 0.41 Pa at ×4, 0.30 Pa at ×8, 0.21 Pa at ×16, 0.08 Pa at ×128. Odr codes run from Hz240 ( 0x00 ) down to Hz0_125 ( 0x1F ); OdrHz() returns the nominal rate. The chip's exact rates differ slightly from the names ( Hz100_2 is 100.299 Hz, Hz50 is 50.056 Hz). IIR filter ¶ data_n = (data_n-1 × c + data_in) / (c + 1) , with c the filter coefficient. The -3 dB bandwidth is the ODR times the normalised bandwidth (datasheet Table 10). docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up a BMP581, their causes and the fix for each, cheapest check first. Start with the DriverError of the failing call ( ToString(r.error) ): Bus and NotInitialized are transport problems; the others mean the chip answered but did not confirm a step. Init() fails ¶ Error Cause Fix NotInitialized Your port's EnsureInitialized() returned false Install or open the bus before Init() Bus No acknowledge at the address, or a dead bus Address from SDO (0x46 low, 0x47 high), pull-ups to VDDIO, CSB tied to VDDIO for I2C InvalidChipId Another part at that address, SDO floating, or the first SPI read after power-up Check the address; on SPI do one dummy read before Init() ( Porting ) NvmNotReady The NVM had not loaded, or nvm_err is set Init() already soft-resets once when STATUS reads 0. Wait at least 2 ms (t_powup) after power-up; if it persists, the part is faulty NvmCommandError nvm_cmd_err left over from an earlier NVM command Soft reset, then Init() again SoftReset() fails ¶ Error Cause Fix Bus over I2C The chip does not acknowledge the reset command and your port reports it Count the write of 0xB6 to CMD as sent ( Porting ) PorSoftReset over SPI The reset returned the chip to I2C mode, so the INT_STATUS read was the invalid switching read Do a dummy read after the reset in the port PorSoftReset Something else read INT_STATUS in between (reading clears it) Do not poll INT_STATUS from another task during the reset Readings ¶ Symptom Cause Fix The values never change The chip is in standby or deep standby Check the result of Configure() or SetPowerMode(PowerMode::Normal) One new value, then nothing Forced mode: one conversion, then standby Set forced mode again per sample, or use normal mode DataReady() never turns true Another reader clears INT_STATUS first, or the chip is not converting Read INT_STATUS in one place only; check the power mode Pressure reads 0 Pressure disabled ( pressure_enable = false ) or ReadSample(false) Enable pressure in OsrOdrConfig odr_valid is false The oversampling pair does not fit the ODR period; the chip runs with ×1 / ×1 or ×2 / ×2 Lower the oversampling or the ODR ( Register interface ) Noisy pressure Low oversampling, or air movement Raise pressure oversampling, enable the IIR filter ( SetIir() ), shield the port from drafts Offset of tens of pascals Solder drift (±30 Pa) or self-heating Compare against a reference once after assembly; keep the sensor away from warm parts SPI only ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Two-byte settings come back wrong The port sends [reg] [d0] [d1] ; SPI writes do not auto-increment Send one address byte before each data byte Every read is shifted by one byte The port drops a "dummy" byte the BMP581 does not send Take data from the byte right after the address Works until the first soft reset A soft reset selects I2C again Dummy read after the reset Next ¶ Hardware has the pins and bus settings; Porting the transport rules.
